subject: Banking
title: AI-Powered Credit Scoring
description: A 60-second lesson on AI-Powered Credit Scoring.

hook.text: AI can analyze 10,000 data points to predict default risk. Traditional scores use fewer than 20.

buildup.text: Machine learning models use bank transaction data, utility payments, and employment history — data FICO ignores.

discovery.text: AI scoring can approve borrowers who FICO rejects. People with thin credit files but steady income become visible.

twist.text: AI models are black boxes. Even their creators can't fully explain why a specific applicant was denied.

climax.text: AI scoring is more accurate but less transparent. Better predictions come at the cost of explainability.

punchline.text: 10,000 data points vs. 20. More accurate, less explainable.

quiz.question: What is the main concern with AI credit scoring?
options: Models are black boxes that can't explain denial reasons

details.summary: AI-powered credit scoring uses machine learning algorithms to analyze thousands of data points beyond traditional credit history, including transaction patterns, employment data, and digital behavior, to predict repayment probability more accurately.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional credit scores miss billions of creditworthy people. AI models can assess borrowers with thin or no credit files, potentially democratizing access to credit while raising concerns about algorithmic fairness and transparency.
takeaways: AI models analyze thousands of variables versus FICO's handful of factors
Alternative data helps score borrowers invisible to traditional systems
Algorithmic bias and lack of explainability create regulatory challenges

faq.question: How is AI credit scoring different from traditional scoring?
faq.answer: Traditional scores use five factors from credit bureau data. AI models process thousands of data points including transaction patterns, employment stability, education, and digital footprints. They find complex patterns that simple scoring formulas miss.

faq.question: Can AI credit scoring discriminate against protected groups?
faq.answer: Yes. If training data reflects historical discrimination, AI perpetuates it. Models may use variables that correlate with race or gender as proxy discriminators. Rigorous bias testing and regulatory oversight are essential to prevent this.
